requirement_text.REQ-073: Port the user-management handler group of src/api/routes/identity.zig (1,868 lines / 23 handlers total -- too large for one agent turn, split four ways across REQ-073..076 along R-Co's own handler boundaries). This requirement takes five handlers: handleCreateUser (L21), handleListUsers (L101), handleGetUser (L130), handlePatchUser (L149), handleUpdateUserStatus (L303). Backing domain logic already exists and is NOT rebuilt here: REQ-015..021 built Letflow.Identity, and REQ-063 made users a per-schema table. Read lib/letflow/identity.ex's actual public functions and route to them; if a handler needs a domain function that does not exist, add the thin function there rather than inlining a Repo query in the handler, and say so in the completion report. Every response goes through REQ-066's builders, every list through REQ-067's cursor pagination, every body through REQ-068's validation, every action through REQ-069's UsersGroupsRolesManage permission check, and every query through REQ-072's scoped prefix. SECURITY (INV-2): a user representation must never serialise password material, a token secret, or an OIDC refresh token, and field selection happens server-side before serialisation -- not by the client omitting fields. Build the response map explicitly (or derive Jason.Encoder with an explicit :only list); do not encode the Ecto struct wholesale, which is how an added column silently becomes an exposed field later.

WF-02 Step 00 — Git setup for REQ-073 (Identity routes 1/4 -- user CRUD and status).

Procedure per docs/agents/protocols/GIT_SETUP.md:
1. git checkout main
2. git pull --ff-only origin main — STOP and FAIL if non-fast-forward
3. git checkout -b feature/WF02-REQ073-20260822
4. git branch --show-current — must equal feature/WF02-REQ073-20260822
5. git push -u origin feature/WF02-REQ073-20260822

This is the first requirement to actually exercise the whole S4 chain end-to-end (REQ-066 response builders, REQ-067 pagination, REQ-068 validation, REQ-069 authorization, REQ-072 tenant scoping) against a real route, mounted into lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex (currently a stub per REQ-070). Full WF-02 pipeline warranted given the security-critical acceptance criteria (INV-1/INV-2/INV-5 all named explicitly).

Key constraints to carry into Step 1: domain logic already exists in Letflow.Identity (REQ-015..021, REQ-063) and must not be rebuilt -- handlers route to existing functions, only adding a thin new domain function if a genuine gap is found (and reporting that explicitly, not silently). The response serialization must use an explicit field allowlist (INV-2) -- never Jason.Encoder deriving from the whole Ecto struct, since an added column would then silently become an exposed field. Every write must go through REQ-069's UsersGroupsRolesManage permission check with the database verified unchanged on a 403 (not just the status code). Every query must use REQ-072's scoped_repo_opts/1, and the cross-tenant-404 test must demonstrate REQ-072's actual mechanism, not a new one.

Complete the handoff: set status COMPLETED, fill result.git_evidence with branch_name and push_status, set next_action to 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 1)'.
